item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Sep 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Sep 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Sep 3 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Curiosity Lab — Thu Sep 3, 4:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
September Theme: Entomology Day: Thursday Time: 4 - 5:45pm Recommended Ages: Designed for children ages 6 - 10, but siblings are welcome. Location: WonderLab Cost: Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Curiosity Lab is an after-school, free play program for kids ages 6-10 years. Children are invited to explore, experiment, and engage in hands-on sensory activities at their own pace. No instructions, no pressure-just curiosity-driven play. Held in WonderLab \(or sometimes outdoors weather permitting\), the space is set up for exploration with a variety of rotating materials and stations. There will be one main activity/installment/manipulative for the month that will be brought out every Thursday. This will rotate with the month and the month's theme.
Source: Limestone Post

item.title: Conversation Partners: Application Open — Thu Sep 3, 5:00 PM — Online
item.description:
In our conversation partners program, you can practice a language one-on-one with a native speaker—and make a new friend!
We will match you with an IU Bloomington student or staff member who can help you learn a language that interests you, and who wants to learn your language. You and your partner will talk and write in both languages. Because your partner will be a native speaker, you will learn how to use the language in daily conversation. You will learn about each other’s culture, too. The matching process is based on the number of applicants and range of spoken languages.
You and your partner will meet at least once a week during the semester. You can meet whenever and wherever you want. Feel free to try out locations other than campus buildings, such as coffee shops, American or international restaurants, parks, or the IU Art Museum.

item.title: PTO Call Out Meeting — Thu Sep 3, 6:00 PM — McNutt Central Quadrangle - C018
item.description:
Interested in financial markets, investing, or learning how professional traders approach the markets? Come join us for the Indiana University Proprietary Trading Club Callout Meeting, where we’ll introduce our organization, explain what proprietary trading is, and show you how you can get involved. Our club is built around education, teamwork, competition, and hands-on market experience. Members will have the opportunity to learn about market analysis, trading strategies, risk management, and portfolio management through paper trading and simulated trading competitions—so you can develop your skills without risking real money. No prior trading experience is required. Whether you’re completely new to financial markets or already have experience trading, there will be opportunities to learn, compete, and contribute. Come meet the founding team, learn about our vision, and find out how you can become part of the organization.
Hosted by: Proprietary Trading Organization

item.title: Animal Hour / Dive Deeper — Fri Sep 4, 3:00 PM — Wonderlab
item.description:
September Theme: Environmental Science Day: Friday Times 3 - 4pm Recommended for: All ages Event Price Free for Members / Free with Museum Admission Get closer to the wild side with Animal Hour and Dive Deeper! These weekly programs let you chat with WonderLab's animal experts, discover what it takes to care for creatures from around the globe, and meet snakes, lizards, insects, arachnids, and more-up close and out of their habitats. Animal Hour takes place on most Fridays, while Dive Deeper happens on the last Friday of each month at WonderLab's stunning coral reef aquarium. Type of Activities Animal Hour: Meet our animal ambassadors. Explore different environments. Dive into ecology and evolution. Type of Activities Dive Deeper: Interactive demonstrations.

Micro Dino Dig \(Best for ages 6 and up\) Excavate mini dinosaur skeletons from the Cretaceous Period while learning real fossil recovery techniques and how scientists study ancient life. item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Tue Sep 8 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Tue Sep 8 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Tue Sep 8 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers
